issues.description: AlterTableStatementSegment no longer accepts multiple comma-delimited alterations in one statement
issues.detail: The outer Delimited(...) wrapper was replaced with OneOf(...). Previously TSQL allowed combined alterations like 'ALTER TABLE x ADD col, DROP COLUMN y' (which the removed test fixture exercised). The new structure only permits a single alteration clause per ALTER TABLE. While SQL Server docs are ambiguous on cross-action combinations, this is a parsing regression for any users relying on the prior behavior.

issues.description: Removed valid ALTER TABLE test case without justification beyond 'invalid'
issues.detail: The deleted fixture 'ALTER TABLE dbo.doc_exc ADD column_b ... CONSTRAINT exb_unique UNIQUE, DROP COLUMN column_a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS column_c' is taken from Microsoft's own sp_help docs example. Calling it 'invalid' in the PR description is debatable; if it's actually valid TSQL, this PR silently drops support for it. Worth verifying against MS docs before merging.

issues.description: IdentityGrammar allows signed increment but SQL Server requires increment to be non-zero signed integer separately
issues.detail: Adding SignedSegmentGrammar to both seed and increment positions is correct for permitting negative values. However, the grammar now also accepts patterns like '+5, +1' which is fine, but no test covers a negative increment (e.g., IDENTITY(100, -1)). Consider adding a fixture for negative increment to lock in the intended behavior.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE accepts NumericLiteralSegment without documented justification
issues.detail: The _default_language grammar now accepts NumericLiteralSegment in addition to quoted/naked identifiers. SQL Server's DEFAULT_LANGUAGE expects a language name (e.g., us_english) or an lcid via separate syntax. A bare numeric literal as a language is not standard syntax per MS docs. No test fixture exercises the numeric case, so its inclusion looks speculative.

issues.description: DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS only applies to first item in delimited list
issues.detail: In the new DROP / Delimited(Sequence(CONSTRAINT, IfExistsGrammar optional, ObjectReferenceSegment)) structure, the inner CONSTRAINT keyword is marked optional. This means 'DROP CONSTRAINT a, b' parses (b without CONSTRAINT keyword) which matches the test fixture, but also permits 'DROP a' alone with no CONSTRAINT keyword at all, which is invalid TSQL. The optional grouping should likely require CONSTRAINT on the first item.

issues.description: Test fixture for table variable index uses lowercase 'index' but no end-of-statement terminator
issues.detail: The new fixture in declare_table_type.sql omits the trailing semicolon and GO. Other fixtures in the file use them. Minor inconsistency that doesn't affect parsing but reduces clarity of intent across the test file.

review.summary: The PR adds several useful TSQL parsing improvements (table variable indexes, CREATE LOGIN options, negative identity seeds, multi-DROP). The main concern is the restructure of AlterTableStatementSegment from Delimited(OneOf(...)) to a bare OneOf(...), which removes support for combining different alteration types in one statement and required deleting a fixture lifted from Microsoft's docs. A few smaller grammar permissiveness questions exist around DEFAULT_LANGUAGE accepting numeric literals and DROP CONSTRAINT making the CONSTRAINT keyword optional. Overall direction is good but the alter table change deserves verification before merge.
